items.summary:
On November 25, 2026, we released versions 19.6.2, 19.5.9, 19.4.11 for GitLab Community Edition (CE) and Enterprise Edition (EE). These versions contain important bug and security fixes, and we strongly recommend that all self-managed GitLab installations be upgraded to
one of these versions immediately. GitLab.com is already running the patched version. GitLab Dedicated customers do not need to take action. GitLab releases fixes for vulnerabilities in patch releases. There are two types of patch releases:
scheduled releases and ad-hoc critical patches for high-severity vulnerabilities. Scheduled releases are released twice a month on the second and fourth Wednesdays.
For more information, please visit our releases handbook and security FAQ .
You can see all of GitLab release blog posts here . For security fixes, the issues detailing each vulnerability are made public on our issue tracker 90 days after the release in which they were patched. We are committed to ensuring that all aspects of GitLab that are exposed to customers or that host customer data are held to
the highest security standards. To maintain good security hygiene, it is highly recommended that all customers
upgrade to the latest patch release for their supported version. You can read more best practices in securing your GitLab instance in our blog post. Recommended Action We strongly recommend that all installations running a version affected by the issues described below are upgraded to the latest version as soon as possible . When no specific deployment type (omnibus, source code, helm chart, etc.) of a product is mentioned, it means all types are affected. Security fixes Dependency updates Recent patches to upstream dependencies bundled with GitLab have been backported or updated for multiple vulnerabilities: Git ( CVE-2026-105437 ): backported to GitLab versions 19.2.11, 19.1.11, 19.0.12, and 18.11.15 (previously included in 19.5.4, 19.4.6, and 19.3.8 ). Ruby ( Ruby security advisory ): backported to GitLab versions 19.3.10, 19.2.11, 19.1.11, 19.0.12, and 18.11.15 (previously included in 19.6.1, 19.5.8, and 19.4.10 ). GitLab has also remediated CVE-2026-129975 , a double free in GPGME, through multiple fixes, all of which are included in GitLab versions 19.6.2, 19.5.9, 19.4.11, 19.3.10, 19.2.11, 19.1.11, 19.0.12, and 18.11.15: The GPGME library bundled with GitLab Linux packages has been patched to fix the double free. Ruby-GPGME (the gpgme gem) has been updated to 2.0.27. OpenPGP input is now validated before it is passed to GPGME as an additional mitigation. NGINX ( NGINX release notes ): updated to 1.31.9 in the Linux package (Omnibus) and GitLab Docker images built from the package in versions 19.6.2, 19.5.9, and 19.4.11. Please note : GitLab Helm Chart and GitLab Operator installations using the deprecated NGINX Ingress controller are also affected. This controller is deprecated and has been disabled by default since 19.0. The upstream NGINX Ingress no longer receives security patches so we strongly recommend migrating to Envoy Gateway or an external Ingress controller. An updated NGINX controller will ship in an upcoming chart release. Extended backports are an exception and do not reflect our standard maintenance policy . Table of security fixes Title Severity Exposure of Sensitive Information issue in dependency proxy authentication impacts GitLab CE/EE Medium Improper Validation of Specified Quantity in Input issue in on-call rotation length API impacts GitLab EE Medium Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling issue in Sentry error tracking client impacts GitLab CE/EE Medium Improper Neutralization of Special Elements issue in Service Desk quick action redaction impacts GitLab CE/EE Medium Exposure of Sensitive Information issue in Work Item REST API CI job token scope validation impacts GitLab CE/EE Medium Server-Side Request Forgery issue in MCP server OAuth token endpoint handler impacts GitLab EE Medium Use of Weak Hash issue in mer
